notes:
Account snapshot: Verdant is a large omnichannel retailer exploring Redwood Dedicated for live chat + personalization reranking across web and mobile. Primary driver = predictable unit costs and latency at peak holiday windows. Very sensitive to outages hitting checkout flows; PCI scope and data residency (US-only) are gating items.

Recent cadence:
- 2026-02-12: Exec intro (FF id ff_20260212_verdant_exec_call). Overview of Dedicated value props. Customer: "we need guarantees during holiday spikes or we lose revenue".
- 2026-02-20: Initial technical discovery with infra/network. Confirmed VPC peering required; internal network team to provide egress IPs.
- 2026-03-04: Deep-dive with infra + ML platform (FF id ff_20260304_tech_deepdive). Benchmarks reviewed.
- 2026-03-08: Pricing follow-up + legal pre-screen.

Key technical notes (from SE call):
- Workloads: reranking (model: open-llama-13b variant), support chat (smaller 7B chat model), nightly embedding jobs for personalization.
- Latency targets: web chat p95 < 250ms, p99 < 400ms for 1-2 turn interactions; reranking tail latency p95 < 120ms. Throughput target: sustained 800 qps across region during peak; burst to 2k qps for 10m windows.
- Reserve planning: initial recommendation = 8x A100-equivalent GPUs per primary region + 3x standby in secondary region for cross-region failover. Customer asked for guidance on right-sizing quantized instances vs full fp16 for reranking.
- Reliability design discussed: automatic cross-region failover (active-primary, passive-secondary), weighted routing by latency, and model-variant fallback chain: primary (full fp16 13B), fallback-1 (int8 13B quantized), fallback-2 (7B chat variant) to preserve SLOs under saturation. SE noted KV cache warmup implications and cold-start penalty on failover.
- SLA asks: 99.95% uptime for Dedicated control/serving plane during business hours; 40ms median latency improvement SLAs were requested for reranking—legal flagged as too prescriptive.
- Observability: Verdant cares about per-route token-level cost & per-model p95/p99 dashboards for chargeback to product teams.

POC plan / milestones:
- Week 1 (2026-03-22): Provision Dedicated pool in us-east-1 with 8 GPUs, mirror in us-west-2 with 3 GPUs (standby). Validate VPC peering; share peering guide. (Action: Carlos to open NET-2048 ticket with infra contact).
- Week 2: Synthetic load tests (throughput ladder): 200, 500, 1k, 2k rps for reranking; measure p50/p95/p99 and GPU utilization. Capture KV cache hit rate impact.
- Week 3: Inject failure (region failover drill) and measure end-to-end failover time and latency delta. Test model variant fallback sequencing under saturation.
- Week 4: Security review and PCI scoping; handoff to legal for final SLA negotiation.

POC acceptance criteria (customer-specified):
- Reranking p95 < 140ms under sustained 800 qps; p99 < 300ms under same load.
- Failover time (cold swap to secondary region) < 90s for routing + KV cache rehydrate within 5 minutes acceptable if fallback chain keeps critical flows alive.
- Demonstrated cost model with optimize suggestions reducing per-request token cost by >=20% via batching/quantization without >3% degradation in rerank quality (A/B measured).

Commercial / SLA negotiation notes:
- Verdant legal pushing back on 'latency SLA with financial penalties' — prefers uptime SLA + defined remediation credits. They want a carve-out for force majeure and network-layer incidents.
- Pricing: customer prefers commit-based reserved capacity with monthly true-ups. Seeking clarity on standby cross-region billing (hot standby vs cold standby). Need to model cost of 3 standby GPUs in secondary region vs rapid burst pricing.

Risks & escalations:
- Network peering delay will block the PoC start. Work with NET-2048.
- Cold KV cache on failover may produce high latency spikes for first 100-500 requests; mitigation = model-variant fallback to 7B chat model + proactive cache sync strategy (discussed).
- Legal wants latency SLOs expressed as targets not financial penalties; AE to propose hybrid SLA: uptime SLA 99.95% + performance objectives with credits tied to availability windows.

Quotable customer lines:
- "If we can't get predictable tails during Black Friday, it's a non-starter."
- "We'd pay for standby if failover is guaranteed under 90s and our cart flows stay intact."

Open action items:
- Carlos to deliver detailed GPU sizing note and quantization tradeoffs (due 2026-03-15).
- Samantha to circulate proposed SLA draft to Verdant legal by 2026-03-12.
- SE + Verdant infra to sync on VPC peering checklist; NET-2048 assigned.

Next steps summary: finalize reserved GPU counts and standby billing model, run cross-region failover PoC week of 2026-03-22, iterate SLA language with legal.
